short_description: Non-canonical FirstPersonEmbodiment research layered on accepted CH9.6, now evaluating one transient held-item presentation state across first- and third-person views.
purpose: Evaluate first-person hands, third-person held-item visibility, clothing-visible viewmodels, independent left/right grip UX and low-latency item-selection presentation without reopening frozen CH9.6 and without weakening authority over concrete item actions.
expected_outcome: A separate research lab can render two first-person hands, switch the local active hotbar slot without a durable Item Graph round-trip, project the same selected item onto the third-person avatar right hand from one transient presentation state, clear both views on an empty slot, and keep concrete item mutations server-authoritative.
current_stage: FPE-R2 S1 — shared transient held-item state and third-person right-hand presentation
progress_note: FPE-R1 core interaction evidence is now sufficient to move forward: the full focused suite passed cleanly on the Fix8 line, continuous movement and Tab are smooth, hotbar selection is instant CLIENT_LOCAL_PRESENTATION with zero durable Item Graph command/checkpoint, and empty-slot selection clears the first-person hand immediately. The user explicitly authorized advancing without making the remaining graphical equipment-drag verification a blocker; the focused equipment result policy remains green, but real CHARACTER_EQUIPMENT_NETWORK_APPLY_FAILED normalization is not claimed graphically accepted and is retained as a non-blocking follow-up. R2/S1 adds HeldItemPresentationState, a transient non-authoritative state keyed by hand, plus ThirdPersonHeldItemPresenter. The presenter attaches a presentation-only proxy to a normalized right-hand Skeleton3D bone through BoneAttachment3D when available and degrades to an AvatarYawRoot-local fallback anchor when no recognizable hand bone exists. The proxy is placed only on the accepted world render layer so first-person camera-layer isolation remains intact. QuaterniusFirstPersonEmbodimentFix9 makes the shared held state the presentation fan-out point: an occupied local hotbar slot updates both the existing first-person viewmodel and the third-person world proxy; an empty slot clears both. Item identity is still read from the installed canonical replica, slot selection remains transient/local, and concrete item mutations remain on accepted M7/CH9 server-authoritative paths. A synthetic Godot 4.7.1 double run has already validated the BoneAttachment3D right-hand path plus world-layer/default-layer isolation. No accepted CH9.6 runtime file is modified.
last_accepted_checkpoint: CH9.6 Playable Network Equipment Lab FOCUSED_ACCEPTED + POST_ACCEPTANCE_PC0_NON_RED @ e547ba52a440e72cc02c6bbe449edaf160bae7ab
next_stage: Operator updates the dedicated detached FPE worktree and runs RUN_FPE_RESEARCH_TESTS.ps1. Two new mandatory R2 gates must pass: FPE R2 shared held-item state and FPE R2 third-person held-item presenter, followed by the existing performance and graphical scene-load gates now bound to quaternius_first_person_embodiment_fix9.gd. Then run PLAY_FPE_RESEARCH.ps1. Graphical acceptance: select an occupied hotbar slot in first person, press C, verify the same item proxy is visible at the world avatar right hand and follows avatar animation/movement; press C back and verify no duplicate world proxy leaks into the first-person view; select an empty slot and verify both views clear immediately; repeated 1..0/C switching must not reintroduce frame stalls. If the bone grip transform is visibly misaligned but follows the correct hand, record it as R2 pose-tuning rather than an authority failure. After S1 acceptance, proceed to R2/S2 item viewmodel catalog + grip profiles, then real hand skeleton/pose work. Canonical world grabbing still requires a separate authority/network contract frontier.
